steps.name: Russell
steps.text: I understand the situation.

steps.name: Russell
steps.text: My concern is, will this information also cross the desk of the General Chamber of Commerce as we are speaking?

steps.name: Adeptus Messenger
steps.text: I expect so. Something on this scale cannot be covered up completely. The G.C.C. will find out.

steps.name: Adeptus Messenger
steps.text: Intel from multiple sources indicates a high likelihood that something abnormal is happening to the Kolossal Prime Vein, and that Ursus is facing an energy crisis.

steps.name: Adeptus Messenger
steps.text: This is corroborated by the recent movements of the First Army on the border... it's certainly cause for concern.

steps.name: Adeptus Messenger
steps.text: We do not know if the energy issues will spread to other regions, nor how Ursus may react.

steps.name: Russell
steps.text: Has there been any official communication from Grypherburg?

steps.name: Russell
steps.text: In the face of such a crisis, the empire's first reaction is to hide the truth, rather than seek cooperation. Their stance is clear as day.

steps.name: Russell
steps.text: A dying beast is a dangerous one. Even without its energy advantage, the Ursine war machine remains terrifying.

steps.name: Russell
steps.text: We have defeated many foes. We are not afraid of war. But we must be even more vigilant about threats from within.

steps.name: Adeptus Messenger
steps.text: You are concerned that the G.C.C. will use this as leverage against the Adeptus?

steps.name: Adeptus Messenger
steps.text: Even they must know the threat we will face if Ursus chooses to expand at this time. Kazimierz cannot afford another incident!

steps.name: Russell
steps.text: Do not underestimate the merchants' thirst for profit.

steps.name: Russell
steps.text: They're already making their move. The invisible war already began when they framed their first innocent campaign knight.

steps.name: Russell
steps.text: Fetch me Liam. Quickly.

steps.name: Russell
steps.text: And where is the scion of Nearl these days?

steps.name: Crumbling Soldier
steps.text: Enough! Stop blowing it up! Do you want the whole mountain to collapse?!

steps.name: Crumbling Soldier
steps.text: Don't you understand, mudak? There's nothing here! Not even one chunk of Originium! It's all dried up! Gone!

spans.text: There's nothing here! Not even one chunk of Originium! It's all dried up! Gone!

steps.name: Despairing Officer
steps.text: Shut your trap! We must keep digging! This isn't the Far North... the ore in the east isn't gone! We just need to get it out first—

steps.name: Despairing Officer
steps.text: 'Find the Originium'! Those are our orders!

steps.name: Crumbling Soldier
steps.text: Well, you can hang us all then, because those orders aren't happening!

steps.name: Crumbling Soldier
steps.text: Ivan's gone blind and I'm deaf in one ear! Better to hang than have all my organs turned to mush by the bombs!

steps.name: Crumbling Soldier
steps.text: Turn us Infected and bury us in the mountains for all I care! Maybe you'll get the Originium growing again that way!

steps.name: Crumbling Soldier
steps.text: Gosudar-batyushka... have mercy on us... have mercy on Ursus...

spans.text: ... have mercy on us... have mercy on Ursus...

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: ...That concludes my report.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: Intercepted communications indicate that the Third Army has received news and announced a ceasefire with the Seventh. Only mobile units remain on standby.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: Where was the explosion?

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: In the wilderness of Central, roughly 2300 km in a straight line from our front lines with the Fourth Army, with no nomadic cities making their winter transit nearby.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: But the scattered settlements in the area were not evacuated in advance. Rumors are that the people and animals were annihilated instantly, leaving behind only strange-colored soil and ash... it must have been incredibly powerful.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: Has the First Army really developed such a terrible weapon?

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: Stand by for further instructions from Command.

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: The Marshal will make the right decision. Until then, as soldiers of the 6th Artillery Regiment of the Second Army's 2nd Division...

steps.name: Officer
steps.text: We will continue to stand against the traitors outside Grypherburg.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: ...Here ends the Grand Duchess's message.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: The last batch of supplies has been delivered, and what information we have on the First Army's new weapon is included in the letter.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: Her Imperial Highness wishes to communicate that this is the full extent of the help that the Far North can provide to the Fourth Army.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: We have fulfilled our end of the bargain. We pray that you do not forget yours, even in the current stalemate with the Second Army.

steps.name: Sullen Soldier
steps.text: I understand. But I hope Her Imperial Highness sees the present situation clearly.

steps.name: Sullen Soldier
steps.text: The conservatives maintain an iron grip over the Council. Backed by the First Army's research, they deny our legitimate claims, our desire to make Ursus great again.

steps.name: Sullen Soldier
steps.text: Time is precious. We will be handing over the nation if the Fourth Army does not achieve the expected aim, and Bresk will hardly be immune if that happens.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: It is not my place to respond on behalf of Her Imperial Highness, but I shall deliver your message faithfully to her.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: Perhaps I could also tell you an old fable, on her behalf.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: The north wind and the sun made a wager on who could get a passing traveler to remove his cloak—

steps.name: Sullen Soldier
steps.text: Escort the honorable herald out.

steps.name: Sullen Soldier
steps.text: Make sure she leaves the base and delivers my message to Bresk safely.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: I'm afraid I have another important matter to attend to on this trip, and will not be returning to Bresk immediately.

steps.name: Messenger
steps.text: I wish you the best of luck. For the glory of Ursus.

steps.name: Sullen Soldier
steps.text: For the glory of Ursus.

steps.name: Hoarse Voice
steps.text: Get lost...

steps.name: Hoarse Voice
steps.text: Get lost!

steps.name: Hoarse Youth
steps.text: Hah... you brought this on yourself.

steps.name: Hoarse Youth
steps.text: You can blame your own insolence.
The young man kicks away the body of the soldier whose throat he just cut, and walks toward the depths of the command center.
The path leading from the deck is littered with bloody bodies, some of which are still twitching. None of the onlookers dare come any closer.

steps.name: Dignified Soldier
steps.text: Anatoliy.
Footsteps. The crowd quickly disperses.
Against the crowd, a pair of boots steps through puddles of blood, stopping only at the sound of metal clanging against blade.
The soldier gazes down at the young man.

steps.name: Dignified Soldier
steps.text: Are you done fooling around?

steps.name: Dignified Soldier
steps.text: Then put your sword down.

steps.name: Dignified Soldier
steps.text: As I've told you before, while you're free to punish those who anger you, showing your rage is simply showing your weakness.

steps.name: Dignified Soldier
steps.text: It is disgraceful, Anatoliy.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: But you've imprisoned me here. While I'm in pain and life has lost all meaning, you just keep me locked up here!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You would not even allow me to witness the birth of Kushkina.

spans.text: You would not even allow me to witness the birth of

steps.name: Dignified Soldier
steps.text: It's for your own safety.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Safety? Hah, safety!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I'm in the heart of the First Army's territory under your great leadership, Marshal Buterina! Is there any place in Terra that is safer?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Yet you would not allow me to step out, not even onto the deck...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Have I become your prisoner just because I have Oripathy? Am I no longer your son, no longer a glorious soldier of Ursus?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Nothing has changed, Anatoliy. I treat you as I always have.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Then let me go! I want to go to Zelgrad. I want to patrol and watch over my city as I always have—as you promised!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Silent again. You're going back on your word, aren't you?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Get someone to clean up, Yasha. As usual.

steps.name: Diligent Servant
steps.text: Yes, madam.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Mother!

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Yes, synochek, I promised you that Zelgrad will be yours. But not yet.

spans.text: , I promised you that Zelgrad will be yours. But not yet.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: You must not leave my sight until your condition is stable. Do you understand?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: No, I don't!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: If you won't let me go, I'll keep killing with this sword that you gave me until there's no one left to guard me. These kozyols wouldn't dare raise a finger against me anyway—

spans.text: If you won't let me go, I'll keep killing with this sword that you gave me until there's no one left to guard me. These
wouldn't dare raise a finger against me anyway—

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: I said, until your condition is stable. Once it is, you can go and do whatever you want to do.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You're playing word games now. Have those handsome Grypherburg bureaucrats changed how you feel about words?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I should have killed them all.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: I captured that Cautus who claims to heal Oripathy.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Her companions were all Infected, as the rumors say. They feel no pain and show no symptoms.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: I think it is worth seeing her, even if she's a fraud.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You would show my pain and weakness to a fraud?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Of course not.
The soldier touches the blade at her chest with her finger. Trembling, the young man finally lowers his sword.
Then, the mother pulls her son into a tight embrace.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: If she is truly a fraud, then neither she nor her companions will leave here alive. But if she can truly stabilize your condition, even heal it...

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Then I shall embrace her, as I embrace you now.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: A lowly Cautus who came from nothing will become a member of the glorious First Army. Because she helped you.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Mama...

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Wipe your tears, synochek. Our guest will be here soon.

spans.text: . Our guest will be here soon.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Bring her, Yasha.
The blood and gore is quickly cleaned up, and the floor once again sparkles as new.
Heavy, orderly footsteps approach, but there is discordance in the order. A lighter footstep, decidedly out of place, causes everyone to look up.
Its source soon reveals itself.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What—
Neither a middle-aged man raggedly dressed in self-styled piety, nor a well-dressed charlatan.
Just a girl with a delicate frame and eyes wide open, herded along the dark carpet like a burdenbeast.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: She's the one?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What could she possibly do? A stiff breeze could blow her over. She wouldn't even make good firewood.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Do not be deceived by appearances. She is indeed the leader of those vagrants.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: My personal guard found her surrounded by adoring vagrants, as at the Grypherburg trial over two years ago.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: It made our removal of her from the crowd seem shameless and preposterous, just like that trial.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You would compare her to the Yurodstvo?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Enough of that. As long as she can help you, I do not care what she is, whether she's a peasant or the Yurodstvo.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Come forward.
The girl shakes her head hesitatingly without moving her feet.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: Are my companions being taken care of?

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: I want to make sure of that.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: You certainly have nerve.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: I only hope to protect my companions.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: You must recognize that you are in no position to bargain.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: This is your last chance. Come forward.
The Cautus seems to recognize the situation and comes forward as instructed, but Anatoliy begins backing off hastily.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Anatoliy?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: She's Infected! Why doesn't she heal herself, if she can heal the Infected?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: She's a fraud, Mother. I don't want to waste time on such fruitless endeavors. I don't have time—

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Take it back.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Mother?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Take it back! You must not say such things. You have time. You'll get better. You must.
The tall woman turns to the girl and peers into her eyes.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: You will heal my son, as you have healed those vagrants.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: If you can heal him...

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: I, Svetlana Ulyanova Buterina, Marshal of the First Army, vow that the First Army shall protect you and your companions for the rest of my days.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: I have to assess his condition, but my presence seems to bring him discomfort?

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: How can I heal him if I can't even touch him?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: As if a little distance would be a problem if you really had the power to heal Oripathy!
The young man turns his head, as though trying to hide the Originium crystals on his cheeks in his hair, refusing to even look at the girl, much less approach her.
The Cautus girl seems to make up her mind. She takes one look at the commander who forcibly 'invited' her here, then approaches the young man.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: I take you at your word, madam...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Stay away from me, peasant!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: If you take one more step towards me—

a.text: Then you will become what you hate the most.

spans.text: Then you will become what you hate the most.

a.text: You trampled upon what little dignity we had left, Generalik, just because you have a marshal for a mother, never tasting the mud and blood of true battle...

spans.text: You trampled upon what little dignity we had left,
, just because you have a marshal for a mother, never tasting the mud and blood of true battle...

a.text: You should have paid for your arrogance long ago!

spans.text: You should have paid for your arrogance long ago!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Get away! Get away from me!!

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Anatoliy, put down the sword—
The Cautus does not stop. The blade grazes her neck, leaving a small wound.
The young man stumbles backward, covering his face with his hand, as though he is the one wounded.
A sudden, violent flare-up of Oripathy, or just painful memories awakened by the sight before him?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I'm not—I didn't—

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: ...Please, calm down...

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: It'll be over soon.
The young man has no room to back off further. When he is about to fall, the girl reaches out and takes the taller youth in her arms.
Both of them fall to the ground. The young man's trembling hands let go of his sword; no more angry words come from his pale lips.
The pain has overcome him.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Argh—

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: Your condition is serious...

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: And you're starting to hyperventilate.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: Follow the rhythm of my breathing, and let my words help you rediscover the feeling of full lungs.
The Cautus touches his cold, tense fingers and sees the black crystals emerging from flesh, hard and sharp as their host.
She puts her hand on the young man's forehead, her voice soft and gentle as she guides his breathing.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: *exhale*

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: 'Believe. Believe in our life.'

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: 'Believe in our body and mind, believe in every beat of our heart, believe in every inhale and exhale.'

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: 'Believe that we...'

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: '...are the source of all strength.'

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: *cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: You are just someone in pain.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I... I don't need your pity—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I don't need the pity of an Infected, of all people...!

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: This is not pity, only sorrow.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: For I cannot cure your Oripathy.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: ...Fraud...

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: The only thing I can do...

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: Is soothe your pain in this life.
As the black Originium on the surface of the young man's body fades and changes, the menacing expression on his face softens.
His eyes remain closed, but his heaving chest has calmed.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: Hence, we pass over to the other side.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: Where there is no pain, no sorrow.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: The land of eternity.
